cards.explanation: The word is "soon," friends. The LORD says, "…for My salvation is coming soon, and My righteousness will be revealed." (Isaiah 56:1) That's the reason He gives for maintaining justice and doing what is right. I like a promise that doesn't come with a long waiting room.

The answer is the Sabbath. The blessed man "…keeps the Sabbath without profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil." (Isaiah 56:2) That's a man who holds fast to what is right. The Sabbath shows up again in this passage, so keep an eye out for it, friends.

The foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD should not say, "The LORD will utterly exclude me from His people." (Isaiah 56:3) This is about a foreigner who has already joined himself to the LORD, and the LORD says he shouldn't say it. I'd say that's a man who needed to hear some good news.

The answer is sons and daughters. The LORD says the memorial and name He gives is "…better than that of sons and daughters." (Isaiah 56:5) He gives it "…in My house and within My walls…" That's the LORD talking, friends, and I'm not about to add anything to that.
The answer is False. The LORD says, "I will give them an everlasting name that will not be cut off." (Isaiah 56:5) That is a name with no end. It goes far past a lifetime, friends.

The LORD says He'll bring them to His holy mountain. "I will bring them to My holy mountain and make them joyful in My house of prayer." (Isaiah 56:7) He is the One doing the bringing, bakers. That's a warm invitation for the foreigners who join themselves to Him.

The word is "joyful." The LORD says, "I will bring them to My holy mountain and make them joyful in My house of prayer." (Isaiah 56:7) Picture the foreigners joyful in the house itself, friends. Now that's a welcome.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on My altar…" (Isaiah 56:7) That is said about the foreigners who join themselves to Him. Accepted, friends. That's the word.
The answer is all the nations. The LORD says, "…for My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations." (Isaiah 56:7) That's a wide door, friends. I never get tired of hearing it.

The answer is False. The Lord GOD, who gathers the dispersed of Israel, says, "I will gather to them still others besides those already gathered." (Isaiah 56:8) He says there are still others, friends. No "that's all, folks" here.
